workload.model: S106B arm M (tag s106b-final model.py), ordinary PyTorch in examples/adaptive_memory.py
workload.optimizer: Muon (NS5 BF16, momentum 0.95, gain 5) + AdamW (0.9, 0.95, 1e-8), wd 0.1, clip 1.0, warmup H/16 + cosine to 10%, lr 3e-3, eta 1
workload.native_precision: FP32 model/derivatives (strict, no TF32); BF16 Newton-Schulz inside Muon exactly as the donor

native_gates.reference: FP64 eager autograd of the same formulation on the same state (H100 FP64), and the donor's unchanged Engine._update applied to the native gradients
native_gates.gradient_rule: per parameter: native rel_l2 vs FP64 <= max(ratio x FP32-eager rel_l2 vs FP64, floor)
native_gates.optimizer_rule: update delta (new - old) rel_l2 vs donor update on identical gradients; Muon bound reflects BF16 Newton-Schulz accumulation-order rounding; FP32 moments/momentum <= state_rel
native_gates.causality: prefix losses (runtime count k) bitwise unchanged under edits of bytes from chunk j on for k <= j-1; changed for k >= j
native_gates.repeat: same state and data: loss, gradients and new parameters bitwise identical
native_gates.counts: runtime counts 0, 1, chunks/2, chunks use the same binary and the same loss/gradient gates
native_gates.fault_sensitivity: FP64 detach_write / read_after_write / future_label mutants must differ from the correct gradients by rel_l2 > 1e-3 (>= 100x the gradient floor)
native_gates.finite_differences: FP64 central differences of the independent donor model along 6 random unit directions vs FP64 autograd of our formulation: rel <= 1e-6

controls.conventional: unchanged S106B Engine (vendored cops4_a/s106b): FlexAttention SWA, torch.compile, one CUDA graph per update

arms.fp32: matched arithmetic, autocast off, TF32 off

controls.validity: FP32 controls: update deltas within the native gradient/optimizer bounds of FP64 on the same state; BF16 arms: the donor's qualified practical policy, reported with their FP64 error

learning_gate.protocol: S106B stream seed 106140, H updates of the frozen recipe from the same init, held-out E-slice mean CE (nats/byte) evaluated by the donor forward in FP32 for every arm
learning_gate.rule: native FP32 E-loss within max(0.03 nats/byte, 1.5 x |conv bf16 - conv fp32|) of conventional FP32; all losses finite

timing.clock: complete changing-state update, CUDA events around graph replay / native launch, inputs staged before the start event
timing.rounds: each arm in a fresh process; native and controls repeated in two rounds on one H100
timing.memory: torch peak allocated bytes in the arm's process (setup + timed updates) and native arena/library bytes
timing.setup: native: CPU capture + lowering + nvcc build receipts, plus GPU library/runtime load; conventional: compile + capture (warm caches recorded separately)
